payload.evidence_to_check: Experimental results tables, dataset descriptions, and backbone specifications. Look for comparisons against strong baselines on large-scale datasets and consistency of performance gains across different model sizes.
payload.failure_mode: Overstating the significance of the contribution by relying on small-scale or niche benchmarks that do not reflect the typical deployment scenarios or the true state-of-the-art in the field.
payload.review_heuristic: Assess the magnitude and generalizability of empirical gains by checking if they are demonstrated on standard, large-scale benchmarks (e.g., ImageNet) and with representative model architectures. If improvements are modest or inconsistent on small scales, flag the SOTA claim as weak.
payload.trigger: The paper claims state-of-the-art improvements or practical benefits but validates them only on small-scale datasets (e.g., CIFAR-10) or small backbones (e.g., VGG11).
payload.why_it_matters: Significance (SIGN-SOT) depends on demonstrating substantial and consistent improvements over strong baselines. Small-scale results may not generalize, leading to an overestimation of the work's impact and practical utility.
